 Does this sound familiar?


## You may have a hidden leak if you've noticed…



Most hidden leaks don't announce themselves with a puddle. They show up as small, easy-to-dismiss signals first.



 1

**An unexplained jump in your water bill**Nothing in your routine changed, but the bill did.


 2

**Your water meter is still spinning**Every fixture is off, yet the meter keeps moving.


 3

**The sound of running water behind a wall**A faint hiss or trickle with no visible source.


 4

**A warm spot on the floor**Often a sign of a hot water slab leak underneath.


 5

**Low or dropping water pressure**A sudden change that wasn't there last month.


 6

**Damp carpet, bubbling floors, or musty smell**Moisture is finding its way somewhere it shouldn't.

## What Does A Slab Leak Actually Sound Like?



This is the exact sound signature our acoustic equipment listens for — press play and hear the difference for yourself.





 ▶


### Healthy Pipe Flow



Steady, low, consistent — normal water movement through an intact line.




 ▶


### Pressurized Leak Hiss



A higher-frequency, continuous hiss — the sound of water escaping under pressure.





Synthesized audio approximation for educational purposes. Real acoustic detection uses calibrated listening equipment far more sensitive than the human ear alone.

 Common questions


## What homeowners ask before calling




 How do I know if I have a hidden water leak? +


Watch for a rising water bill with no change in usage, a water meter that keeps moving with everything off, warm spots on the floor, or the sound of running water when no fixtures are on. Any one of these is worth a professional diagnostic.




 Can a leak be found without damaging my home? +


In most cases, yes. Acoustic, electronic, and thermal detection let us narrow the leak to a small, specific area before any concrete or drywall is opened — which is the entire point of diagnosing before repairing.




 How long does leak detection take? +


Most residential leak detection visits take one to a few hours depending on the size of the home, the type of leak, and how accessible the plumbing is. We'll give you a time estimate up front.




 Does insurance cover slab leak detection? +


It depends entirely on your specific policy. We can't make coverage promises, but we can provide clear diagnostic findings and documentation to bring to your insurance company. See our [Insurance Resource Center](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com//insurance/) for more.




 What's the difference between repair, reroute, and repiping? +


A spot repair fixes a single, accessible leak. A reroute avoids a problem section of pipe entirely. Whole-house repiping replaces the system when age or repeat failures make that the smarter long-term option. We'll walk you through which fits your situation after diagnosis — never before.

 Our story


## Why the name "Straight Flush"



In poker, a straight flush is one of the strongest hands you can hold — every card accounted for, nothing left to chance. That's the standard we hold ourselves to on every job: know exactly what you're dealing with before you act.



Too many homeowners get a repair quote before anyone has actually confirmed where the leak is coming from. That approach leads to unnecessary demolition, repeat visits, and repairs that don't solve the real problem. We built Straight Flush around the opposite approach: diagnose thoroughly first, using real detection technology, then explain the options in plain language.



Based in Laguna Niguel and serving Dana Point, San Clemente, and the surrounding South Orange County communities, we treat every home like it's in our own neighborhood — because it usually is. **Lance answers the phone.** We are the specialist for [slab leaks in copper-era homes on expansive clay soils](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com//south-oc-slab-leak-specialist.html).

 How we work


## The diagnostic approach that sets us apart




Most leak detection starts with a guess and a demolition crew. Ours starts with physics.

- **Acoustic leak detection:** Specialized listening equipment pinpoints the sound of pressurized water escaping from a pipe — even through a concrete slab.

- **Thermal imaging:** Infrared cameras show temperature differences from a hot-water leak, narrowing the search area without breaking concrete.

- **Electronic pipe locating / pressure testing:** Confirms which line is leaking and isolates the problem before you pay for a repair.

Once we've pinpointed the leak, we walk you through the honest set of repair options — whether that's a spot repair, a reroute, or a full repipe — with real pricing, so you can make an informed decision.

 How do I schedule leak detection or plumbing service? +

 Do you handle emergency calls? +

# Leak Detection Services | Acoustic & Thermal Detection

> AI-readable Markdown mirror of the canonical HTML page: https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/services/leak-detection.html

[Home](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/) › Leak Detection
 Acoustic · Electronic · Thermal


# A leak you can't see is still a leak we can find.



Hidden leaks waste water and damage homes. Straight Flush finds them with acoustic, electronic, and thermal diagnostics — owner-operated in Laguna Niguel, where Lance answers the phone and we diagnose before recommending repair or repipe.

 [Schedule Leak Detection](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/contact.html)






 The direct answer


## What is water leak detection?



Water leak detection uses specialized equipment — acoustic listening devices, electronic pipe locators, and thermal imaging cameras — to identify precisely where a leak is occurring inside walls, under floors, or underground, without needing to open up the entire area first.



It's the diagnostic step that should always happen before a repair quote. Skipping it is how homeowners end up with unnecessary drywall or slab demolition that misses the actual leak.



 Signs you need it



- Rising water bill with no change in usage

- Water meter still spinning with everything off

- Sound of running water behind a wall or under a floor

- A warm spot on flooring (possible hot water slab leak)

- Dropping water pressure

- Damp carpet, bubbling floors, or a musty smell









 Our technology


## Three detection methods, matched to your situation




 Acoustic


### Sound-Based Detection



Sensitive listening equipment picks up the distinct sound of pressurized water escaping a pipe underground or inside a wall cavity.



 Thermal


### Infrared Imaging



Thermal cameras detect temperature differences caused by moisture or hot water leaks beneath flooring, invisible to the naked eye.



 Electronic


### Electronic Locating



Sensor-based tracing follows the exact path of a pipe, narrowing down the access point to a precise, small area.









 Our process


## How a leak detection visit actually works



 01

#### Consultation

We discuss your symptoms and history with the property.


 02

#### Visual Inspection

We check all accessible plumbing and fixtures first.


 03

#### Pressure Testing

Isolating which line and zone is involved.


 04

#### Technology Locating

Acoustic, thermal, or electronic tools pinpoint the source.


 05

#### Findings & Options

We explain what we found and your realistic options.

 Leak detection FAQ


## Common questions



 How do you find a leak without cutting into walls or floors? +


We isolate the system with pressure testing, then use acoustic listening equipment to hear the sound of escaping water, thermal imaging to spot temperature changes from hot-water leaks, and electronic locating to trace the pipe's path. That narrows the leak to a small, specific area before any wall, floor, or concrete is opened, so any access needed stays as small as possible.




 What is the difference between leak detection and slab leak detection? +


General leak detection covers leaks anywhere in the system, including walls, ceilings, fixtures, and under floors. Slab leak detection is the same diagnostic approach focused on pressurized water lines running beneath a concrete foundation, where acoustic and thermal tools pinpoint the leak without breaking up the slab.




 Will my insurance cover leak detection? +


Coverage depends on your policy and the cause of the loss. Many policies address the resulting water damage rather than the plumbing repair itself. We document what we find so you have clear evidence for a claim, and our insurance resources cover what to ask your provider.




 How much does leak detection cost? +


Cost depends on the type of leak, how deep it sits, and how accessible the plumbing is, which is why we diagnose before quoting any repair. Lance will walk you through what to expect for your specific situation, and our leak detection cost guide explains the factors that affect price.




 What happens after you find the leak? +


Once we have located it, we explain what we found and your realistic options, including spot repair, reroute, or repipe, and why one may make more sense than another for your home. No repair is recommended before you understand the diagnosis.

[Home](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/) › [Leak Detection](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/services/leak-detection.html) › Slab Leaks
 Our core specialty


# Slab leak detection in South Orange County, CA



Straight Flush is the South Orange County specialist for slab leaks under 1970s–1990s copper systems in expansive clay soils. Lance answers the phone. We use acoustic, electronic, and thermal detection to pinpoint the leak before any concrete is opened.

 [Schedule Slab Leak Detection](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/contact.html)






 Warning signs


## Signs of a slab leak




- A warm or hot spot on the floor with no obvious cause

- The sound of running water when everything is off

- A noticeable rise in your water bill

- Cracks in flooring or baseboards

- Low water pressure throughout the home

- Damp carpet or a musty smell near the slab




 What causes it


## Why slab leaks happen



Most slab leaks in Orange County homes trace back to aging or corroded copper piping, especially in homes built before PEX became standard. Contributing factors include:




- Corrosion from decades of mineral-rich water exposure

- Pipe abrasion against concrete or rebar over time

- Soil shifting common to coastal and hillside Orange County lots

- Original installation quality issues









 Do this first


## The 30-minute water meter test



This is the most reliable check you can run yourself before calling anyone.




- Turn off every fixture, appliance, irrigation zone, and pool fill valve.

- Write down the meter reading, or take a photo of it.

- Wait 20–30 minutes without using any water.

- Check the meter again. Any change means water is leaving your system somewhere.

- If it moved, close the supply valves to your toilets and irrigation and repeat. If the meter still moves, the leak is most likely in a supply line, which is where acoustic detection comes in.




More detail: [what a moving water meter tells you](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/water-meter-still-moving-everything-off.html).



 Right now


## Should you shut off your water?



It depends on how fast water is escaping.




- **Shut off the main valve now** if water is coming up through the floor, the meter is spinning fast, or a warm spot is spreading.

- **Suspect a hot water line?** Closing the cold-water valve on top of a tank water heater stops flow to the hot side while the rest of the house keeps water. Set the heater to vacation or pilot while it’s off.

- **Meter only creeping?** You usually don’t need to go without water, but don’t wait long. A running leak keeps adding to your bill and to the damage.




Not sure where your shutoff is? See our [emergency plumbing checklist](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/emergency-plumbing-checklist.html).








 How we find it


## Acoustic detection: listening for the leak itself



Pressurized water escaping a pipe underground makes a distinct sound. Our acoustic equipment isolates that sound through the slab, narrowing the leak's location to a small, specific area before anyone picks up a hammer. It is the same diagnose-first process we bring to older homes across South Orange County — see how we approach [slab leaks in 1970s–1990s Orange County homes](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/south-oc-slab-leak-specialist.html).




 Step 1


### Isolate the Line



Pressure testing confirms which water line is affected, hot or cold, and which zone of the home it runs through.



 Step 2


### Acoustic Sweep



Listening equipment is used across the suspected area to pinpoint the loudest, most consistent point — the leak itself.



 Step 3


### Confirm & Mark



Thermal imaging cross-checks the finding when applicable, and the exact spot is marked for the smallest possible access point.









 Your options after diagnosis


## Repair, reroute, or repipe?






### Spot Repair



Best when there's a single, accessible leak in an otherwise sound plumbing system. The fastest, least invasive fix.





### Reroute



A new line is run around the problem section of pipe, avoiding it entirely rather than repairing it in place.





### Whole-House Repipe



The right call when copper throughout the home is aging or leaks have repeated. We install modern PEX and explain why, honestly.









 Pricing


## What slab leak detection and repair cost



You get a specific number before any work starts, and no surprise charges. The repair path is the biggest factor: a spot repair costs least, a reroute sits in the middle, and a whole-house repipe is the larger investment that deals with aging copper once.



We recommend the option that matches what we actually find, not the biggest invoice. See the [slab leak repair cost guide](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/guides/slab-leak-repair-cost.html) and [leak detection cost guide](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/guides/leak-detection-cost.html).



 What moves the price


### Five things that change the number




- Size of the home and how many areas are suspect

- Hot or cold line, and whether more than one line is leaking

- What sits on top of the leak: tile, hardwood, carpet, or cabinets

- Repair path: spot repair, reroute, or repipe

- Whether you need documentation for an insurance claim










 Slab leak FAQ


## Common questions



 What causes a slab leak? +


Most slab leaks come from aging or corroded copper pipes, poor original installation, shifting soil, or abrasion where a pipe rubs against concrete or rebar over time.




 How do you find a slab leak without breaking concrete? +


Acoustic listening equipment detects the sound of pressurized water escaping underground, and thermal imaging can reveal temperature differences from hot water leaks — together narrowing the leak to a small, specific area.




 Should I repair, reroute, or repipe? +


A single, accessible leak is often a candidate for a spot repair. Repeated leaks or aging copper throughout the home may make a reroute or full repipe the smarter long-term option — something we discuss after diagnosis, never before.




 What is the difference between a slab leak and an underground water leak? +


A slab leak is an underground leak, but not every underground leak sits under the slab. Supply lines can also run beneath the yard, driveway, or patio. We pressure test and isolate to confirm which line is losing water, then use acoustic listening and line tracing to determine whether the leak is under the foundation or outside it. That distinction changes both the repair and the cost.




 Can you detect a slab leak under tile, hardwood, or laminate? +


Yes. Acoustic listening works through finished flooring because it tracks the sound of pressurized water escaping the pipe rather than looking at the surface. Thermal imaging is most useful on hot water leaks and can be limited by thick flooring, so acoustic detection usually leads. The goal is to narrow the leak to a small area before any flooring or concrete is opened.




 How long does slab leak detection take? +


Most detection visits take one to a few hours, depending on the size of the home and how quickly the source is isolated. We go over your options on the spot. A spot repair is often done the same day or the next, a reroute usually takes one to two days, and a whole-house repipe a few days. More in [how long slab leak repair takes](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/how-long-does-slab-leak-repair-take.html).




 Will my flooring have to come up? +


Not always. Acoustic detection narrows the leak to a small spot, so any opening is as small as possible. A reroute often avoids opening the floor at all by running a new line through the attic or walls. If a spot repair under tile or hardwood is the best option, you will know where the access point is and roughly how big it will be before you decide.




 Should I shut off my water if I think I have a slab leak? +


Shut off the main valve right away if water is coming up through the floor, the meter is spinning fast, or a warm spot is spreading. For a suspected hot water leak, closing the cold-water valve on top of a tank water heater stops flow to the hot side while the rest of the house keeps water. If the meter is only creeping, you usually do not need to go without water, but get it diagnosed soon. See [what to do first](#before-you-call).




 Can a slab leak come back after it is repaired? +


The repaired section itself should not be the problem. But copper tends to corrode throughout a system, so if one section of an older line has failed, other sections of the same age often are not far behind. Two or more leaks within a few years is a common point to consider a reroute or repipe. New PEX greatly lowers the risk, though no plumbing system is leak-proof forever. More in [why some homes get repeat slab leaks](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/multiple-slab-leaks-same-house.html).




 Does homeowners insurance cover slab leak detection and repair? +


Coverage varies by policy and is never something we can promise. Many policies handle the resulting water damage and access to the pipe, while the pipe repair itself is sometimes treated as a maintenance item. A [documented diagnosis](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/insurance/documentation-checklist.html) with the affected line, location, and findings typically makes the claim conversation much easier. See [does insurance cover slab leaks](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/insurance/does-insurance-cover-slab-leaks.html) for more detail.










 By city

 What we repair

 A real example


## Pressure problems aren't always where you'd expect



We've traced pressure issues on buried lines back to a pressure regulator installed on the wrong end of the run — downstream instead of at the source. Moving it upstream solved what looked, at first, like a much bigger problem. That's the value of diagnosing before repairing: sometimes the fix is smaller than it looks, and sometimes it's in a different place than expected.








 Plumbing repair FAQ


## Common questions



 Why does my water pressure keep dropping? +


Common causes include a failing pressure regulator (PRV), mineral buildup in pipes, or a hidden leak somewhere in the system. We diagnose which one applies before recommending a fix.




 Is a running toilet worth fixing right away? +


Yes — a running toilet can waste a significant amount of water and add up quickly on your water bill, and it's usually an inexpensive repair.




 Do you repair or only replace fixtures? +


We repair whenever a repair is the sound long-term choice, and only recommend replacement when the fixture or part is genuinely beyond a reasonable repair.

# Whole-House PEX Repiping | Copper Line Removal

> AI-readable Markdown mirror of the canonical HTML page: https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/services/pex-repiping.html
> Section: Services
> Summary: Whole-house PEX repiping and copper line elimination in Laguna Niguel, Dana Point & San Clemente. Honest guidance on when repiping actually makes sense.

---
[Home](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/) › [Leak Detection](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/services/leak-detection.html) › PEX Repiping
 When repair isn't the answer anymore


# Whole-house PEX repiping, explained honestly before it's recommended.



PEX repiping replaces aging, leak-prone copper lines throughout a home with modern, corrosion-resistant piping — but it's only the right call after diagnosis shows it's actually needed.

 [Ask If Repiping Is Right For You](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/contact.html)





 The direct answer


## What is whole-house PEX repiping?



PEX repiping means removing or bypassing a home's old metal (usually copper) water lines and replacing them with cross-linked polyethylene (PEX) piping. PEX resists the corrosion and pinhole leaks that plague aging copper, and it's flexible enough to route with fewer joints — fewer joints means fewer future failure points.



We only recommend a full repipe once diagnosis shows it's the smarter long-term choice — not as a default answer to a single leak.



 Why homeowners choose it



- Repeated slab leaks in aging copper lines

- Corrosion visible at multiple fixtures

- Discolored water or metallic taste

- Preparing an older home for resale

- Wanting to stop patching the same system repeatedly








 Copper vs. PEX


## Why PEX has become the modern standard



 Durability

### Corrosion Resistant

PEX doesn't corrode the way copper does, which removes the leading cause of slab leaks in older Orange County homes.


 Installation

### Fewer Joints

Flexible runs mean fewer fittings behind walls and under slabs — and fewer fittings means fewer places a leak can start.


 Value

### Long-Term Cost

Fewer repeat service calls over the life of the system, even though the upfront investment is real.









 PEX repiping FAQ


## Common questions



 Do I need to repipe my whole house, or just part of it? +


It depends on the age and condition of your existing lines. Sometimes a partial reroute solves the problem; sometimes the whole system is due. We'll tell you which applies after diagnosis, not before.




 How long does a whole-house repipe take? +


Most residential repipes are completed in one to a few days depending on the size of the home and wall/slab access, with water restored at the end of each working day whenever possible.




 Is PEX safe for drinking water? +


Yes. PEX piping is certified for potable water use and is the standard choice in new residential construction today.

 Signs you need service


## When to call about your water heater



 1

**No hot water, or it runs out fast**A failing heating element or sediment buildup is often the cause.


 2

**Rumbling or popping sounds**Usually sediment hardening at the bottom of the tank.


 3

**Water pooling around the base**Could be a tank leak — worth an inspection before it worsens.


 4

**Discolored hot water**Often a sign of corrosion inside an aging tank.


 5

**Your unit is 8–12+ years old**Most tank water heaters are nearing the end of their service life by then.


 6

**Rising energy bills**An inefficient or failing unit can quietly cost you more every month.

 Water heater FAQ


## Common questions



 Is it worth switching to tankless? +


It depends on your household's hot water usage, existing gas/electric setup, and how long you plan to stay in the home. We'll walk through the real numbers with you rather than a blanket recommendation.




 How long do water heaters typically last? +


Traditional tank water heaters usually last 8 to 12 years, while tankless units can last considerably longer with proper maintenance.




 Can a water heater leak cause a slab leak? +


A failing water heater can leak at its base or connections, but a true slab leak involves a pipe under the foundation. If you're not sure which you're dealing with, we can diagnose it directly.

 Should I repair or replace my water heater in an older Laguna Niguel home? +


It depends on the unit's age and what failed. A thermostat, element or valve is usually worth repairing; a leaking tank or a unit past roughly 8 to 12 years usually isn't. We diagnose first and tell you which one makes sense — including when a repair is all you need.




 My hot water runs out fast — is it the water heater or a leak? +


It can be either. Sediment or a failing element is common, but in Laguna Niguel's copper-era slab homes a leak on the hot-water line under the floor can also make the heater run nonstop. We check for both before recommending a new unit.

## Water heaters in Dana Point homes



Salt air and coastal humidity are hard on anything metal that's exposed — and many Dana Point water heaters sit in garages or exterior closets. California requires water heaters to be strapped against earthquake movement. When we replace a unit, we install it with proper seismic strapping and bring the connections up to current requirements.

 Does salt air shorten the life of a water heater in Dana Point? +


Coastal air mainly attacks exposed metal — gas connectors, vent pipes, valves and fittings — especially on units in garages or exterior closets. Regular checks of those parts can catch corrosion before it causes a leak or a venting problem.




 My water heater is leaking at the bottom — do I need a new one? +


Not always. Water at the base can come from the relief valve, a loose connection or a nearby pipe rather than the tank. A leaking tank does need replacement, so we confirm the source before quoting either.

# Slab Leak Detection in Laguna Niguel, CA



Straight Flush Plumbing & Leak Detection is headquartered in Laguna Niguel, and slab leaks are our core specialty. We pinpoint the leak with acoustic, electronic and thermal tools before any concrete, tile or flooring is opened.

 Who to call in Laguna Niguel


## Who does slab leak detection in Laguna Niguel?



Straight Flush Plumbing & Leak Detection finds and repairs slab leaks in Laguna Niguel. We're an owner-operated plumbing company based in Laguna Niguel — it's where we've diagnosed more slab leaks than anywhere else — and owner Lance answers the phone himself at [(949) 374-6524](tel:+19493746524).



## Slab leaks in Laguna Niguel homes



Much of Laguna Niguel was built in the 1970s–90s, from Bear Brand to Niguel Summit, and a large share of those homes still run their original copper water lines through or under the slab. Decades of mineral-rich water, pipe rubbing against concrete or rebar, and South OC's expansive clay soils are the usual reasons those lines eventually pinhole.



The early signs are easy to miss: a warm spot on the floor, the sound of running water with everything off, a water bill that jumps for no reason, or a water meter that keeps moving. Laguna Niguel is served by Moulton Niguel Water District, so your bill history there is a good place to look for an unexplained rise in use.



Before you call anyone, you can run the [30-minute water meter test](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/academy/water-meter-still-moving-everything-off.html). If the meter moves with every fixture and irrigation zone off, water is leaving the system somewhere — and that's where acoustic detection comes in.



 Slab leak services in Laguna Niguel



- Pressure testing to isolate the hot or cold line

- Acoustic leak location through tile, wood or carpet

- Electronic pipe locating to trace the line under the slab

- Thermal imaging to confirm hot-water leaks

- Spot repair, reroute, or whole-house [PEX repipe in Laguna Niguel](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/services/pex-repiping-laguna-niguel.html)

- Written findings to bring to your insurer (no coverage promises)




Same-day appointments are often available, and we take emergency calls 24/7. More on [how we find slab leaks](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/services/slab-leak-detection.html) and [plumbing in Laguna Niguel](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/cities/laguna-niguel.html).







 How we work


## Find the leak first, then a straight answer on repair, reroute or repipe



 1 · Isolate

### Which line is leaking?

Pressure testing confirms whether the hot or cold line is losing water, and which part of the house it runs through.


 2 · Pinpoint

### Listen for the leak itself

Acoustic equipment picks up the sound of pressurized water escaping under the slab; thermal imaging cross-checks hot-water leaks. The spot is marked for the smallest possible opening.


 3 · Decide

### Repair, reroute, or repipe

One leak in otherwise sound copper is often a spot repair. Repeat leaks in aging copper may make a reroute or repipe the smarter call — we explain the trade-offs after diagnosis, never before.

 Who does slab leak detection in Laguna Niguel? +


Straight Flush Plumbing & Leak Detection does slab leak detection and repair in Laguna Niguel.  Why do so many Laguna Niguel homes get slab leaks? +


Many Laguna Niguel homes were built in the 1970s to 1990s with copper water lines run through or under the slab. Over decades, mineral-rich water, abrasion against concrete or rebar, and South Orange County's expansive clay soils wear those lines down until they pinhole.




 Can you find a slab leak in my Laguna Niguel home without breaking up the floor? +


In most cases, yes. Acoustic listening narrows the leak to a small area through tile, hardwood or carpet, and thermal imaging helps confirm hot-water leaks. Any opening is kept as small as possible, and a reroute can often avoid opening the floor at all.




 Will insurance cover a slab leak in Laguna Niguel? +


Coverage depends on your policy, and we can't promise it. Many policies treat the resulting water damage and access differently from the pipe repair itself. We give you written findings — the affected line, location and what we found — to bring to your insurer.

 What are the signs of a slab leak in a Dana Point home? +

 Do coastal conditions in Dana Point affect plumbing leaks? +

# PEX Repiping in Laguna Niguel, CA

 [Call (949) 374-6524](tel:+19493746524)





 Who to call in Laguna Niguel


## Who does PEX repiping in Laguna Niguel?



Straight Flush Plumbing & Leak Detection does whole-house and partial PEX repiping in Laguna Niguel. We're an owner-operated plumbing company based in Laguna Niguel, and because leak detection is our specialty, we can tell you whether you actually need a repipe. Owner Lance answers the phone himself at [(949) 374-6524](tel:+19493746524).



## Repiping Laguna Niguel's copper-era homes



Much of Laguna Niguel was built in the 1970s–90s, and many of those homes still run their original copper water lines. Copper tends to wear throughout a system at the same rate, so when one section of an older line pinholes, other sections of the same age are often not far behind.



That's the point where homeowners start asking about a repipe: two or more slab leaks within a few years, corrosion at several fixtures, discolored water, or simply being tired of patching the same system. PEX resists the corrosion that causes those pinhole leaks, and its flexible runs need fewer fittings — fewer joints means fewer places for a future leak to start.



Not every home needs the whole system replaced. Sometimes a reroute of one problem line solves it. We test and inspect first, then tell you which applies — see [repair vs. reroute vs. repipe](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/guides/repair-vs-reroute-vs-repipe.html).



 Repiping services in Laguna Niguel



- Whole-house copper-to-PEX repiping

- Partial repipes and reroutes of a failing line

- [Slab leak detection in Laguna Niguel](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/services/slab-leak-detection-laguna-niguel.html) before any repipe decision

- New shutoff valves and supply connections at fixtures

- Water restored at the end of each working day whenever possible

 Laguna Niguel repiping FAQ


## Common questions from Laguna Niguel homeowners



 Who does PEX repiping in Laguna Niguel? +


Straight Flush Plumbing & Leak Detection does whole-house and partial PEX repiping in Laguna Niguel. We're an owner-operated company based in Laguna Niguel, we diagnose before recommending a repipe, and owner Lance answers the phone at (949) 374-6524.




 Do I need to repipe my whole Laguna Niguel house after a slab leak? +


Not necessarily. A single leak in otherwise sound copper is often a spot repair or reroute. Repeated leaks, corrosion at several fixtures or discolored water are signs the whole copper system may be due. We tell you which applies after diagnosis, not before.




 How long does a PEX repipe take in Laguna Niguel? +


Most residential repipes take one to a few days, depending on the size of the home and wall and slab access. We restore water at the end of each working day whenever possible.




 Is PEX better than copper for older Laguna Niguel homes? +


For homes with aging copper, PEX is usually the better long-term choice: it doesn't corrode the way copper does, and its flexible runs need fewer fittings, which means fewer places for a leak to start. It's also certified for drinking water and standard in new residential construction.

 Our approach


## Diagnose before we clear



A single slow drain is often a simple, local clog. Recurring or whole-house drainage issues usually point to something further down the line — which is where camera inspection earns its keep, confirming exactly what's happening before any cutting or digging is discussed.



We explain what the camera shows in plain language, then walk through every reasonable option.








 Drain services FAQ


## Common questions



 Do I need a camera inspection for a slow drain? +


Not always. A single, isolated slow drain is often solved with standard cleaning. Camera inspection becomes valuable when the problem is recurring, affects multiple fixtures, or involves the main sewer line.




 What causes a main sewer line backup? +


Common causes include tree root intrusion, aging or collapsed clay pipe, grease buildup, and, in older Orange County neighborhoods, simple pipe age.




 Is hydro jetting safe for older pipes? +


It can be, but pipe age and material matter. We'll assess the line's condition first and recommend the appropriate cleaning method rather than defaulting to the most aggressive option.

# Emergency Plumber in Orange County — We Answer the Phone.



A burst pipe, slab leak, or sudden water heater failure can't wait until Monday. Straight Flush Plumbing provides 24-hour emergency plumbing across Orange County. Call now and reach a real person who knows what to do.


 [Call (949) 374-6524](tel:+19493746524)
 [Schedule Non-Emergency](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/contact.html)



For emergencies, always call directly. For non-urgent service, use the form.








 Know when to call


## What counts as a plumbing emergency?



A plumbing emergency is any situation where water is actively damaging your property, you cannot stop a leak, or a critical system has completely failed. The following situations warrant an immediate call.






### Burst Pipe



A pipe that has ruptured can release hundreds of gallons of water in minutes. Shut off your main water supply immediately and call. Every minute counts.





### Active Slab Leak



If you can hear water running constantly with everything off, feel a warm spot expanding on your floor, or see moisture wicking up through flooring, you likely have an active slab leak that needs same-day attention.





### Major Water Leak



Any leak you cannot control with a shutoff valve, or one causing visible water damage to walls, ceilings, or floors, is an emergency. Mold growth begins within 24–48 hours.





### Water Heater Failure



A water heater actively leaking or flooding the utility area needs immediate service. A failed tank can release significant water before the supply line is shut off.





### No Water to the Home



A sudden complete loss of water pressure—with the street supply confirmed on—may indicate a major main line break. This requires diagnosis before damage progresses.





### Sewer Backup



Sewage backing up into your home through floor drains or toilets is a health hazard and requires urgent attention. Do not use any drains until the blockage is cleared.










 While you wait


## What to do before the plumber arrives




 Step 1


### Shut Off the Water



Find your main shutoff valve—usually near the water meter or where the main line enters the home—and close it completely. This stops the majority of damage immediately.



 Step 2


### Stay Clear of Hazards



If water is near an electrical panel, outlets, or appliances, keep your distance and do not attempt repairs yourself. Water and electricity are a dangerous combination.



 Step 3


### Document the Damage



Take photos and video of the leak, standing water, and any visible damage before cleanup. This documentation is valuable for your insurance claim and helps us assess the situation on arrival.



 Step 4


### Call Straight Flush



Call [(949) 374-6524](tel:+19493746524). Lance or a member of the team will walk you through the situation over the phone and dispatch immediately.

# Why South OC Homes Get Slab Leaks | 1970s–90s Copper Guide

> AI-readable Markdown mirror of the canonical HTML page: https://straightflushplumbingoc.com/south-oc-slab-leak-specialist.html
> Section: Specialty
> Summary: Why 1970s–90s South OC homes get slab leaks: aging copper, expansive clay, hard water — and how acoustic and thermal detection finds them before demolition.

---
[Home](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com//) › South OC Slab Leak Guide
 Homeowner guide


# Why 1970s–1990s South Orange County homes get slab leaks



Aging copper under the slab, expansive clay soil and hard water add up to more slab leaks in South OC homes of this era. This guide explains why, what to watch for, and how a leak gets found without breaking up your floor. Already think you have one? Go straight to [slab leak detection in South Orange County](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com//services/slab-leak-detection.html).








## The South OC problem most generic plumbers under-diagnose



Large parts of Laguna Niguel, Mission Viejo, Dana Point, San Clemente, Aliso Viejo, and nearby communities were built in the 1970s through 1990s with copper water lines under the slab. Those pipes have now lived through decades of hard water and, critically, **expansive clay soils** that swell and shrink with moisture. The result is a higher rate of pinhole leaks and slab leaks than newer PEX or carefully engineered systems see.



A generalist who defaults to large exploratory cuts can cost you far more than a precise acoustic and thermal diagnosis. Straight Flush was built around the opposite approach: listen and measure first, open only what is necessary.



## How these leaks get found without demolition



Finding a slab leak is a process of elimination, done before anyone opens concrete or tile:




- **Pressure testing** confirms which line is losing water, hot or cold, and which part of the house it runs through.

- **Acoustic listening** picks up the sound of pressurized water escaping, and works through tile, hardwood and laminate.

- **Thermal imaging** shows the warm footprint of a hot water leak on the floor above it.

- **Electronic line locating** traces where the pipe actually runs under the slab.




Used together, these narrow the leak to a small spot, so any opening is as small as possible. Often the floor never needs opening at all, because a reroute through the attic or walls bypasses the bad section. The full step-by-step is on our [slab leak detection page](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com//services/slab-leak-detection.html).



## Warning signs to watch for



Warm or hot spots on the floor, a water meter that moves with everything off, unexplained high water bills, the sound of running water when no fixtures are on, or damp areas at the base of walls are all reasons to get a professional diagnosis. In South OC copper-era homes, waiting often turns a small slab leak into a larger repair.



**Call (949) 374-6524.** Lance answers. We serve Laguna Niguel and all of South and Central Orange County.



[Book slab leak detection](https://straightflushplumbingoc.com//services/slab-leak-detection.html)

 How it works


## What this score actually measures



The Home Plumbing Health Score looks at five of the most common risk factors for hidden leaks and slab leaks: the age of your plumbing system, recent water bill trends, your repair history, water pressure, and any current warning signs you've noticed.



Each answer is weighted based on how strongly it correlates with leak risk in the homes we've diagnosed throughout Orange County. It's a self-assessment, not a diagnosis — think of it as a first, free filter to help you decide whether a professional visit is worth scheduling.



 Why we built this



- Most homeowners don't know they're at risk until a leak is already causing damage

- A few simple questions can reveal patterns worth paying attention to

- It's free, instant, and requires no signup

- If your score comes back low, we'll tell you honestly — and if it's high, we'll tell you that too









 Common questions


## About this tool



 How accurate is the Home Plumbing Health Score? +


It's a directional self-assessment based on common risk factors, not a diagnostic tool. It's designed to help you decide whether a professional inspection is worth scheduling, not to replace one.




 Is the Home Plumbing Health Score free? +


Yes, completely free with no signup required. It takes about 60 seconds to complete.




 What do I do if I get a low score? +


A lower score means several common risk factors are present in your home. We'd recommend scheduling a professional leak detection visit to get an accurate, confirmed answer rather than relying on the self-assessment alone.

 Do you serve my neighborhood in Laguna Niguel? +


Yes — Straight Flush Plumbing & Leak Detection is headquartered in Laguna Niguel — this is where it all started, and where we've diagnosed more slab leaks than anywhere else. We serve all of Laguna Niguel and the surrounding South and Central Orange County communities, and Lance personally answers the phone.




 Can you find a slab leak in a Laguna Niguel home without tearing up my floors? +


In most cases, yes. We use acoustic listening equipment, electronic amplification, and thermal imaging to pinpoint the leak to a small, specific area before any concrete, tile, or drywall is opened — so any access needed stays as small as possible.




 How fast can you get to a leak in Laguna Niguel? +

 What are the warning signs of a hidden leak in a Laguna Niguel home? +


An unexplained jump in your water bill, a water meter that keeps moving with everything off, the sound of running water behind a wall, a warm spot on the floor, or dropping pressure. Any one of these in a Laguna Niguel home is worth a professional diagnosis before it becomes water damage.
